newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX stutters at end of record-chasing week.
newsitem.headline: German DAX stutters at end of record-chasing week.

text.p: German shares flagged in bourse dealings on Friday, ending slightly lower after a week that saw the market set fresh records on the back of a liquidity upsurge, despite alarming slides on Wall Street.

The 30-share DAX index closed the floor session down 9.88 at 3,795.41, virtually unchanged from last Friday's close at 3,788.27 but not far off the psychologically key 3,800 level it breached several times during the week.
"Things have calmed down now and I think some investors are worrying that once the end of the second quarter is behind us, no more money will come in," said a Frankfurt trader.
"But there is no fundamental reason for us to fall off these levels."

Rotating interest in all the main blue chip sectors had supported the market through the week, with banks, chemicals and carmakers all coming in for attention and helping offset factors like Monday's 2.5 percent slide in the Dow Jones index.
On Friday, eight DAX shares rose and twenty two fell.
Dealers noted that Deutsche Telekom AG, trading ex-dividend, was unusually firm amid positive sentiment generated by its shareholder meeting Thursday.
The share ended up 50 pfennigs at 43 marks.
Dealers noted that the market was keen on car shares as Volkswagen AG, boosted on Thursday by a restatement by Merrill Lynch of a strong buy recommendation, advanced 28 marks to 1,305 marks.
Luxury carmaker BMW AG was also higher on the day, rising five marks to 1,432 marks.
